Hisham on the authority of Ibn 'Amir, and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim, read "yarahu" with sukun on the ha' in both the first and last instances. Ibn Kathir, Hamzah, al-Kisa'i, and Nafi' (as transmitted from him by Warsh), and al-Halwani from Qalun on his authority, read "yarahu" in the first instance; the last instance is a pause sukun. As for one who makes the first sukun, it is according to the dialect of those who lighten, and from it is the poet's saying:

"........... and my two arms longing for him, sleepless."

This dialect was not related by Sibawayh, but al-Akhfash related it. Abu 'Amr alone read with a damma on the ha' in both places, with lengthening. Aban on the authority of 'Asim, Ibn 'Abbas, Abu Haywah, and Humayd ibn al-Rabi' on the authority of al-Kisa'i read "yarahu" with a damma on the ya', meaning the seeing of sight: that he perceives it with his eyes, meaning: (p-٦٧١) he sees its reward and recompense, because past deeds are never seen by the eye. This whole verb, from "ra'aytu" in the sense of "adraktu bi-basari" (I perceived with my sight), has only one object. 'Ikrimah read "khayran yarahu" and "sharran yarahu." al-Naqqash said: it is not seeing by sight; rather the meaning is: it will befall him and reach him.

It is related that this surah was revealed while Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, was eating with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and Abu Bakr stopped eating and wept. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him, "O Abu Bakr, what makes you weep?" He said, "O Messenger of Allah, shall I be asked about the weights of atoms?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, "O Abu Bakr, of what you dislike in this world, the atoms of evil are what you have seen, and Allah will store up for you the weights of the atoms of good."

The "dharrah" is a small, red, thin ant, for which no balance is weighed. It is said that it moves when a year has passed for it. This has been interpreted in the verse of Imru' al-Qays:

"Of the restraint-eyed mares, if a moving one of the dharr crept upon the heel of her hoof, it would have left a trace."

al-Naqqash related that they said: there were two men in Madinah. One of them did not care about the minor sins he committed, and the other wanted to give charity but found only a little, so he was ashamed to give charity. The verse was revealed concerning both of them, as if it were said to one of them: give charity with the little, for the atom's weight of good is seen; and it was said to the other: refrain from minor sins, for the measures of the atoms of evil are seen.

The commentary on Surah [al-Zalzalah] is complete, and praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds.
